column1: # The macOS composing-chord rules, read by both sides: the Swift Shortcuts
# rules from the core (macos-desktop-core-roadmap.md P14) the two coexist,
# and this table is what holds them equal. Every expectation is written by
# hand, never generated from either side.
# Tab-separated. A chord is `<modifiers>|<scalars>`: modifier letters d (⌘)
# c (⌃) o (⌥) s (⇧), then the key's Unicode scalars in hex. `-` is "none".
# A fourth and fifth column name the core's answer and the open parity item
# when the two sides differ today (roadmap § Parity decisions).
#   parse    <stored value>  <chord it reads as | refused>  [core  item]
#   match    <chord>  <event's unmodified characters, hex>  <event modifiers>  <yes | no>
#   resolve  <stored rows: action=value;… | ->  <every row: action=chord | action=- >  [core  item]
# The codec: modifier order, case fold (K6), the two folded keys.
# The typing-key gate: letters, digits, `-` and `;` need ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥.
# Reserved whatever is held (K4): Backspace, Delete, Escape, the arrows and
# E6: a fold that adds a combining mark — the Mac reads the grapheme (not
# ASCII, so not a typing key), the core the first scalar `i`.
# An empty hex field refuses the whole value (E7, settled P11a).
# Matching an event: on its unmodified characters, folded, and on exactly
# Resolution: absent = the default, empty = cleared, unparsable = cleared;
# a chord on two rows stays on the one the user recorded; an emptied commit
# row takes back a free default of its pair, never a key off another row.
